ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Biomedical Sciences studies human health and disease from molecules and cells to organs and populations. Its bachelor combines genetics, cell biology, biochemistry, immunity, anatomy and physiology with research methods and practical work. The third year includes open minor space, a restricted choice and a substantial supervised research thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines human biology and disease with research methods. Two related options emphasise population-health prevention or biomedical foundations with data analysis. Each retains substantial biological and disease content. Social science, economics and computing contribute methods relevant to the chosen emphasis. Specialist histology, omics, embryology, dedicated oncology and the prolonged VU research placement remain important differences.

curriculum.routeLabel: Ordinary bachelor with the experimental thesis
curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC comprises 108 EC prescribed first- and second-year courses, three separate 6 EC restricted choices, 30 EC open minor space and one 24 EC thesis. The curriculum shown includes the first-listed choices and one thesis format. Thesis entry requires all 60 EC from year one and at least 42 EC from year two, an approved project and completed registration. A go/no-go review, scientific report, oral and poster presentations and sufficient research performance apply. The usual first-year study advice threshold is 42 EC, subject to applicable exceptions. Lab safety and the Dutch language test or required remediation are mandatory without extra credit. Programme instruction changed to Dutch in 2026; individual courses may be English.

componentNotes.y1-10: First-listed of three restricted 6-EC year-one choices (Biomedische Wetenschappen en de Maatschappij, Science Communication, Biochemisch onderzoek); selected for this valid pathway.
componentNotes.y2-10: First-listed of four restricted 6-EC year-two choices (Pathophysiology of heart and circulation, Big data, International Public Health, Science Communication).
componentNotes.y3-01: Genuinely open academic 30-EC third-year minor/profiling space; no optional minor is imposed.
componentNotes.y3-02: First-listed of four restricted 6-EC year-three choices in the adopted OER (Epidemiology, Human Neurophysiology, Management of Innovations, Infectious Diseases).
componentNotes.y3-03: Selected 24 EC Experimental thesis: independently conduct supervised laboratory, observational or computer-modelling research in an approved scientific programme; lab journal, scientific report, oral and poster presentations. All 60 EC from year one plus at least 42 EC from year two; enrolment and completed OnStage approval before start. Go/no-go at 4–6 weeks. Professional development sufficient and research 40%, report 35%, oral 20%, poster 5%; each partial grade at least 5.5. February starters have a compulsory poster symposium. Data Analysis is a mutually exclusive alternative, not an additional 24 EC requirement.
